descriptors.definition: Internal audit is an independent appraisal function established within an organization to examine and evaluate internal controls, risk management, and governance processes. It focuses on error prevention and system strengthening to provide reliable financial and operational information to stakeholders.
inclusion: Review of internal control systems
Examination of financial and non-financial records
Process-focused operational evaluations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from external audit by its primary orientation toward internal management and operational governance rather than external reporting.

descriptors.concept_name: Management Functions And Scope Of Internal Auditing
descriptors.definition: Management utilizes internal audit to help ensure resources are optimally used to attain enterprise goals within legal and economic constraints. The scope of internal auditing encompasses systematic reviews of all business processes, covering both financial and operational activities based on underlying risks.
inclusion: Formulating scope and periodicity with the Audit Committee
Reviewing financial and operational business processes
Evaluating managerial functions
exclusion: Unilateral scope determination by the internal auditor without governance consultation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general management execution by functioning as an independent review mechanism rather than direct operational implementation.

descriptors.concept_name: Integrity, Objectivity And Independence Of Internal Auditor
descriptors.definition: Internal auditors must maintain uncompromising independence in mind and appearance, free from undue influences, pressures, or conflicts of interest. They are required to conduct their work honestly, maintain high personal integrity, and remain unbiased when gathering and evaluating evidence.
inclusion: Direct reporting lines to the Audit Committee
Resisting management interference in setting audit scope
Avoiding review of previously managed activities
exclusion: Seeking undue personal benefits or advantages
Allowing prejudice to override professional conclusions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard professional courtesy by requiring strict structural and mental detachment from operational duties.

descriptors.definition: An internal auditor must possess comprehensive multi-disciplinary expertise covering accounting, finance, operational controls, and information technology systems. Strong communication skills and a strict commitment to maintaining information confidentiality are also essential for effective performance.
inclusion: Evaluation of financial and accounting controls
Understanding of ERP systems and software applications
Application of commercial and legal knowledge
exclusion: Disclosure of sensitive organizational information without authorization
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general financial accountants through required proficiencies in operational technology, risk evaluation, and behavioral management.

descriptors.definition: Executing an internal audit engagement requires following a structured five-step sequential process starting with business understanding and planning. This involves assessing regulatory landscapes, analyzing underlying risks, and utilizing approved work plans to test controls.
instrument_references: SIA 310 Planning the Internal Audit Assignment
inclusion: Meetings with key stakeholders and board members
Reviewing IT landscapes and ERP systems
Preparing detailed risk-based audit schedules
exclusion: Performing audit checks without an approved audit plan or scope
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from ad-hoc operational reviews by adhering to a formal, sequential methodology governed by professional auditing standards.

descriptors.definition: Internal audit reporting is conducted in stages, involving assignment-specific reports on findings alongside comprehensive periodic summaries for governance bodies. The auditor must issue clear, well-documented reports based on evaluated evidence while immediately escalating any actual or suspected frauds.
inclusion: Issuing assignment-specific reports to local and executive management
Submitting periodic comprehensive summaries to the Audit Committee
Immediate disclosure of asset misappropriation or fraud
exclusion: Concealing suspected irregularities from executive management
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from broad entity-level quarterly reports by focusing on specific functional assignments and localized operational observations.

descriptors.definition: The internal audit function must continuously monitor the closure of prior audit issues through a formal tracking mechanism for implementation status. The internal auditor evaluates corrective actions taken by management and reports any unresolved or pending matters to those charged with governance.
instrument_references: SIA 390 Monitoring and Reporting of Prior Audit Issues
inclusion: Tracking management implementation of past recommendations
Maintaining cross-referenced draft and final reports
Ascertaining reasons for unacted suggestions
exclusion: Assuming direct operational responsibility for executing management action plans
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial audit testing by focusing specifically on evaluating subsequent remediation efforts tied to historical findings.

descriptors.concept_name: Relationship Between Internal And External Auditors
descriptors.definition: The statutory auditor must examine the scope, effectiveness, and independence of the internal audit function to determine its impact on external audit procedures. While internal and external audit scopes often overlap, statutory auditors evaluate internal audit work to appropriately adjust the nature, timing, and extent of their compliance and substantive testing.
inclusion: Evaluating internal audit staff qualifications and department structure
Assessing internal control reliability for external audit reliance
Modifying external audit testing intensity based on internal evaluations
exclusion: Delegating the statutory auditor's ultimate legal opinion responsibility entirely to internal personnel
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by the external auditor's primary focus on financial statement attestation versus the internal auditor's ongoing internal governance and operational focus.

descriptors.concept_name: Determining Whether, in Which Areas, and to What Extent the Work of the Internal Audit Function Can Be Used
descriptors.definition: External auditors must evaluate the objectivity, competence, and systematic quality control approach of the internal audit function before deciding to use its work. The external auditor is prohibited from utilizing internal audit work if organizational status fails to support objectivity or if technical competence is insufficient.
inclusion: Appraisal of internal control effectiveness
Review of internal audit documentation standards
Assessment of technical proficiency and quality control
exclusion: Using internal audit work when objective safeguards are inadequate
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from direct assistance provisions by focusing on utilizing pre-existing internal audit work products rather than deploying internal staff directly.

descriptors.concept_name: Determining The Nature And Extent Of Work Of The Internal Audit Function That Can Be Used
descriptors.definition: When determining the scope of internal audit work to utilize, external auditors evaluate the relevance of the activities to overall audit strategy and risk assessments. Direct assistance assignments must be carefully structured around judgment levels and the significance of identified threats to objectivity.
inclusion: Assessing amounts of professional judgment required
Evaluating the presence of threats to internal auditor objectivity
Aligning external audit planning with internal findings
exclusion: Assigning internal auditors to make significant audit judgments
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished by restricting direct assistance deployment where high risks of material misstatement demand exclusive external auditor judgment.

descriptors.concept_name: Determining Whether, In Which Areas, And To What Extent Internal Auditors Can Be Used To Provide Direct Assistance
descriptors.definition: External auditors must maintain sufficient involvement in the audit when using internal auditors for direct assistance, retaining sole responsibility for the audit opinion. Internal auditors providing direct assistance must not be assigned tasks involving significant judgments or higher assessed risks of material misstatement.
inclusion: Documenting evaluations of objectivity threats and competence levels
Recording written agreements with entity representatives
Retaining supervisory review work papers
exclusion: Using direct assistance for decisions required to be made by the external auditor under SA 610
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from routine reliance on internal audit reports by involving direct operational support and supervision under external auditor direction.

descriptors.concept_name: If the External Auditor uses Internal Auditors to Provide Direct Assistance on the Audit, the External Auditor shall include in the Audit Documentation
descriptors.definition: When deploying internal auditors for direct assistance, the external auditor is required to maintain comprehensive audit documentation supporting the engagement. This documentation must explicitly record threat evaluations, competence assessments, work allocation bases, written agreements, and supervisory review records.
instrument_references: SA 610 Using the work of Internal Auditor
inclusion: Documenting who reviewed the work and the extent of the review
Archiving working papers prepared by assisting internal auditors
Recording the basis for decisions concerning work extent
exclusion: Omitting supervisory review signatures and evaluation notes from working papers
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard audit work papers by requiring specific tracking and sign-off elements dedicated to the oversight of internal audit staff.
